papers.title: The Gorsky-Oblomkov-Rasmussen conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincar\'e series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to compute the Khovanov skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
papers.abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

papers.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
papers.abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $\rho:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_\rho$ be the energy function on Teichm\"uller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ \rho_{g,h,d}:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ \tau(\rho_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{\rho_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.

papers.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
papers.abstract: We prove that the K\"ahlerness of a finitely presented, residually finite group is not determined by its profinite completion, which answers a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober. In the proof, we give explicit constructions to characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions.

papers.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds
papers.abstract: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.

papers.title: Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces
papers.abstract: We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature. For the almost-positive metrics we describe every zero-curvature plane and prove that the zero-point loci have Hausdorff dimensions exactly $11$ and $23$, respectively. A one-step deformation has, in each dimension, an explicit zero locus with nonempty interior. Further nested deformations reduce it to a measure-zero set while leaving a common codimension-one stratum. The argument combines normal forms for horizontal commuting planes with quaternionic rank conditions and a dimension estimate for commuting compressions of skew-symmetric operators. We also determine the possible degrees of arbitrary free finite quotients of the three flag covers and derive order bounds for fundamental groups when the Euler characteristic is nonzero. We have used ChatGPT-6-astra for mathematical exploration and verified and rewritten all the results.

papers.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
papers.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

papers.title: On the homotopy automorphism group of simply-connected homology $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we compute the group of homotopy equivalences of closed, smooth, simply connected $6$-manifolds whose integral homology groups are isomorphic to whose of the complex projective space $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$, building on computations of their mapping class groups.

papers.title: Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives
papers.abstract: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.

papers.title: Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group
papers.abstract: For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle. As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space. Moreover, using the explicit construction and combinatorial properties of the Farey tessellation, we compute the asymptotics for the critical exponent in the symmetric space and the Hilbert critical exponent as the triple ratio of the triple of flags goes to infinity.

papers.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
papers.abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

papers.title: Compact branch sets and injectivity of proper branched coverings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that a proper continuous open discrete map from the open unit ball $B^n$ onto a domain in $\R^n$ with $n\geq5$ is a homeomorphism whenever its branch set is compact. This answers Vuorinen's question affirmatively in every dimension $n\ge5.$ In dimension four, we also show that, under the additional assumption of quasiregularity, the map is a quasiconformal homeomorphism. Together with the three-dimensional theorem of Kauranen, Luisto and Tengvall, these results answer the quasiregular question posed as Problem~7.66 in the collections of Barth--Brannan--Hayman and Hayman--Lingham in every dimension $n\ge3$.

papers.title: The full length of short pants
papers.abstract: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Rationally Null-homologous Floer Simple Knot
papers.abstract: We prove that every rationally null-homologous Floer simple knot in a closed, oriented, irreducible three-manifold with nonzero Thurston norm is unknotted. The proof combines a cut-and-reglue comparison for extremal Floer groups with Binns's theorem on Floer-minimal knots in balanced sutured manifolds.

papers.title: Embedding Calculus, Goodwillie Calculus and Link Invariants
papers.abstract: We study Goodwillie-Weiss embedding calculus through its relationship with Goodwillie's functor calculus. Specifically, building on a result of Tillmann and Weiss, we construct a functorial complement for \(T_{n}\)-embeddings that takes values in Heuts's categorical \(n\)-excisive approximation of pointed spaces. We also establish an analogue of Stallings' theorem for lower central series in the context of \(T_{n}\)-embeddings of \(P \times I\) into \(D^{d}\) for any compact manifold \(P\). As an application, we show that the embedding tower of string links detects Milnor invariants.

papers.title: Triangulation of orbifolds with corners
papers.abstract: We prove that every compact orbifold with corners admits a triangulation compatible with all its corners: for every $k\ge1$, each connected component of the $k$-corners maps onto the image of a subcomplex, and every open simplex lies in the set of points of a single depth. Faces need not be embedded, and the local groups may permute boundary components. The proof turns the boundary hyperplanes of linear charts into mirrors by means of the squaring map, which, unlike the folding $y\mapsto|y|$, is compatible with smooth changes of charts, and then applies the triangulation theorem for orbit spaces of proper Lie groupoids.

papers.title: Semifree actions and representation varieties
papers.abstract: A group action on a topological space induces an action on the space's representation variety. We determine the fixed point sets of this latter action for semifree group actions on surfaces and circle bundles over surfaces. We also discuss implications for mapping tori of periodic maps.

papers.title: Liftable braid factorizations from line arrangements: Hironaka's relations and a Zariski pair
papers.abstract: We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists. The Artal-Carmona-Cogolludo-Marco Zariski pair gives two such factorizations of the same braid for a single simple branched covering of the disk. Their lifts are Hurwitz inequivalent even up to simultaneous conjugation by page homeomorphisms. The corresponding Milnor fibers fill the same planar contact three-manifold and have the same incidence matrix. They are homeomorphic and lie in distinct strong symplectic deformation classes.

papers.title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
papers.abstract: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

papers.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
papers.abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

papers.title: Rational knots, quivers, and tails of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials
papers.abstract: We use the knots-quivers correspondence to prove that the colored HOMFLY-PT polynomial of a rational knot has a tail and give an explicit formula for calculating the tail in terms of the quiver.

papers.title: Infinitude of integral Hitchin representations of Coxeter polygons
papers.abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a Coxeter $n$-gon($n \geq 9$) group whose boundary parameters are fixed. We construct infinitely many Hitchin $\operatorname{SL}^\pm(3, \mathbb Z)$-representations of a specific Coxeter $6$-gon or $8$-gon corresponding to positive integral points of a generalized Markoff equation.

papers.title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
papers.abstract: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $\gamma\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $\gamma$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times \Sigma_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.

papers.title: Simply connected quotients of fake quadrics
papers.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a short introduction to their arithmetic construction, aimed at low-dimensional topologists, and studies their holomorphic and antiholomorphic quotients and their fundamental groups. The running example in the paper comes from a quaternion algebra over a totally real cubic field. The lattice is generated by three explicit pairs of matrices. A holomorphic involution gives (after resolving the singularities) a simply connected minimal complex surface of general type with $p_g=0$ and $K^2=4$, a smooth $4$-manifold homeomorphic but non-diffeomorphic to $CP^2$ blown up $5$ times. An antiholomorphic involution gives a smooth four-manifold homeomorphic to $S^4$, with a knotted torus as branch locus.

papers.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$. In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.

papers.title: Secondary Stiefel-Whitney numbers and corresponding cobordism groups
papers.abstract: For every relation $R$ between Stiefel-Whitney numbers of closed $(n+1)$-manifolds we consider an associated invariant $\varkappa_R$ of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds with a certain additional structure. For $n=2k-1$ and $R = w_{n+1}+v_k^2$ the invariant $\varkappa_R$ equals the Kervaire semi-characteristic. In addition, we construct the cobordism group $\Omega_n^R$, which extends the unoriented cobordism group $\Omega_n^O$. We show that $\varkappa_R$ is a complete invariant of $R$-cobordism classes of null-cobordant $n$-manifolds. We prove that our invariant $\varkappa_R$ and $R$-cobordism class of manifold are quadratic in the sense of Gusarov-Vassiliev-Podkorytov.

papers.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
papers.abstract: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.

papers.title: $(t,q)$-Series Invariants of Seifert Manifolds
papers.abstract: Gukov, Pei, Putrov, and Vafa developed a $q$-series invariant of negative definite plumbed $3$-manifolds with spin$^{c}$ structures, building on earlier work of Lawrence and Zagier. This was recently generalized to an an infinite family of two-variable $(t,q)$-series invariants by Akhmechet, Johnson, and Krushkal (AJK). We calculate one such series for all Seifert manifolds with $b_{1}=0.$ These results extend a previous theorem of Liles and McSpirit to any number of exceptional fibers and the Reduction Theorem of Gukov, Svoboda, and Katzarkov to the two-variable case. As a consequence, a previous result of Liles and McSpirit on modularity properties and radial limits is enhanced to a larger family of manifolds. We also calculate the infinite collection of $(t,q)$-series invariants for three infinite families of manifolds, finding mixed modularity properties for one such family.

papers.title: On a twisted Singer conjecture
papers.abstract: According to the Singer conjecture, the $L^2$-Betti numbers of a closed aspherical manifold are expected to vanish outside the middle dimension. In this paper, we study a natural analog of the Singer conjecture concerning the vanishing of twisted $L^2$-Betti numbers outside the lower middle dimension. These invariants can be thought of as $L^2$-Betti numbers of an infinite cyclic cover, depending on a first cohomology class. This is related to a previous conjecture by the author, which connects the twisted $L^2$-Euler characteristic to the Thurston norm, and which we prove for a class of closed arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds.

papers.title: The flip symmetry on Khovanov-Rozansky homology
papers.abstract: The flip symmetry on link diagrams induces an involution on Khovanov-Rozansky ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ homology. We prove that this involution is the identity over the integers, generalizing a previous result of Chen and the author. The key ingredients of the proof are (1) a homotopy perturbation argument from a detailed study of the fork twist, which allows us to reduce the computation to planar ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ webs, and (2) the computation of the flip map for planar ${\frak{gl}}_{N}$ webs via diagrammatics of Soergel bimodules. The latter computation can also be interpreted as a naturality result for the half twist action on type $A$ Soergel bimodules, which might be of independent interest.
